newsitem.title: JAPAN: Yokohama Rubber sees 97/98 tyre exports rising 10%.
newsitem.headline: Yokohama Rubber sees 97/98 tyre exports rising 10%.

text.p: Yokohama Rubber Co Ltd said on Monday that its tyre exports are expected to rise by about 10 percent in the business year ending March 1998 from 68,300 tonnes in 1996/97.
"Export demand for tyres in countries in Southeast Asia and the Middle East continues to be robust, partly backed by the yen's weaker tendency," a company official said.
Yokohama Rubber is the second largest tyre maker in Japan.
He said although it was difficult to forecast exports given the volatile currency market, Yokohama was aiming to boost tyre exports by 10 percent this business year.
The official said growth in tyre demand for new cars is likely to be flat as domestic auto output is unlikely to increase sharply this year.
The company announced that sales in the tyre division posted a marginal increase of 0.4 percent to 183.9 billion yen in 1996/97. Its tyre division accounts for 71.9 percent of total sales.
"Although tyre demand increased in 1996/97 led by robust export demand, intense price competition at home offset the sales increase," the company said.
